thread:
maya: quick triage dump for sparrowhawk-v1 quant runs. ran wiki50k holdout (5k queries) comparing fp16 -> 6-bit per-channel (pc) -> 4-bit mixed (pl fallback). sharing condensed metrics + next steps.

jon: drop the numbers pls.

maya: ```
model                recall@1  recall@5  recall@10  silhouette  mean_norm
sparrowhawk-fp16     0.715     0.856     0.895      0.418       12.4
sparrowhawk-6bit-pc 0.712     0.851     0.892      0.411       12.1
sparrowhawk-4bit-mix 0.689    0.829     0.871      0.366       9.7
```

maya: Observations: 6-bit per-channel is within noise (~0.3% @1) and tiny silhouette dip. 4-bit shows ~2.6% absolute drop @1 and a large mean L2 norm reduction for a subset of queries.

liam: which index config?
maya: IVF8192 + HNSW overlay (M=32, efConstruction=220). baseline nprobe=32, I also ran nprobe=64 for 4-bit.

jon: did you try re-scaling or per-vector norm restore?
maya: quick experiment: applying scalar rescale (per-vector multiplier using fp16 statistics) recovers ~0.9% @1 for 4-bit but doesn't close gap. normalizing vectors before indexing helps some but still behind.

eva: any split by query length or entity count?
maya: quick strat: queries<8 tokens: fp16=0.688, 6bit=0.684, 4bit=0.645. queries>30 tokens: fp16=0.744, 6bit=0.742, 4bit=0.736. so short queries are hit hardest.

opsbot: Eval job 1751234567 completed at 1751235120. Logs: s3://redwood-evals/sparrowhawk/1751234567.log :white_check_mark:

liam: could be quant noise affecting head tokens in encoder (short contexts rely on early layer precision). can you run batch=1 encode and also with disable-kv-cache for fairness?
maya: queued batch=1 and disable-kv-cache runs. command used: ```bash
python tools/eval_embeddings.py \
  --model sparrowhawk-v1 \
  --quant 4bit --quant-profile mixed_layer_fallback \
  --dataset wiki50k --index ivf8192_hnsw \
  --nprobe 32 --batch 2048 --metrics recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,silhouette,mean_norm
```

maya: followups: ran nprobe=64 + scalar-rescale for 4-bit: recall@1 improved from 0.689 -> 0.697. batch=1 run still shows a gap.

jon: good to know. what about UMAP / cluster visuals?
maya: UMAP (attached internal): <https://internal/redwood-artifacts/sparrowhawk/umap-4bit-1751234567.png>. 4-bit has a few topic clusters that smear; silhouette drop aligns.

liam: do we have per-class recall (e.g., entity-heavy docs vs generic)? might explain norm collapse on high-entity density items.
maya: started strat by entity density. preliminary: high-entity docs keep norms better; mid-density docs show largest norm compression.

eva: we should decide gating for Dedicated: 6-bit looks safe. 4-bit maybe experimental flag with warnings.

jon: agree. propose: default onboard quant profile = 6bit-per-channel for Dedicated; 4bit locked to opt-in with stricter eval (stratified recall + rerank smoke + UMAP sanity).

liam: actionables: @maya finish batch=1 + disable-kv runs and drop CSV of per-length buckets. @eva add a rerank smoke harness for sparrowhawk to check UX impact. I'll draft a quant policy note for the onboarding doc.

maya: noted. will upload CSV and condensed plot links when done. ETA ~50m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jon: thanks all. reconvene after results. :thumbsup:
